response: Yes, airway surgery has been shown to lower serum lipid levels in some patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Studies have found that surgical treatment of OSA, such as uvulopalatopharyngoplasty (UPPP), can lead to improvements in lipid profiles, including decreased levels of triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, and total cholesterol. However, the extent of these improvements can vary depending on the individual patient and the specific surgical procedure used. Additionally, lifestyle changes, such as weight loss and dietary modifications, may also contribute to improvements in lipid profiles in OSA patients.
